properties.name: On an engine served for others, a signature is the caller's own, checked where the store writes it (#616 fix 4, the enforcement half)
properties.rationale: THE CAUSE, recorded in the LIVE design (not in this branch's store): fact:root-cause-the-settle-rule-guards-the-typed-doors-and-the-generic-writers-go-around-it-2026-09-29, section SCOPE WIDENED 2026-09-30 (Anthony: "record the proper cure in reflow2's generic-writers fix"): an AUTHORED_BY with the approver role is a signature, and every write path recorded one while checking only that the named Contributor exists, so the rule could only be contained per door (flo2 #105, #107 scan argument names). The ruling is dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id, option (e). The capability is cap:an-exposed-server-establishes-who-is-calling-before-intent-can-be-settled (live design). MEASURED FAILING FIRST on a clean origin/main 3a14696 build under the shared build lock (live: fact:eighteen-served-writers-sign-in-another-contributors-name-through-a-registry-2026-09-30): the class test read 117 write tools off the served surface and 18 wrote a signature in another contributor's name through a real registry (acknowledge_defect, acknowledge_gap, acknowledge_gaps, add_decision, add_design_rule, add_requirement, apply_merge, authored_by, collapse_decision, create_edge, create_edges, create_node, create_nodes, delete_edge, draw_edges, import_graph, set_decision_status, set_requirement_status); the undeclared-engine test saw all five settling calls written. Both pass on the fix. flo2 must declare REFLOW2_TRUSTED_GATEWAY=flo2.io on its engine in the same upgrade (flo2 draft PR #106), then drop the argument-scanning stopgaps of flo2 #105 and #107.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: How the engine is served decides who is calling (reflow2-mcp caller.rs, CallerRule). Local (stdio, --shared, --http answering loopback only) is unchanged: no signer is installed. An engine served for others (--registry-root, or --http-allow-host naming a non-loopback host) with --http-trusted-gateway <NAME> / REFLOW2_TRUSTED_GATEWAY takes the caller from the name the gateway puts on each call in _meta["reflow2/writes_for"]; a session's own writes_for names nobody there and the tool refuses it. With nothing declared, or a call the gateway names nobody on, nobody can sign. ENFORCED IN THE STORE, never per tool: reflow2_core::intent::Signer is installed by the write lock for the length of each hold (as #632 installs the acting agent) and asked at the store's one AUTHORED_BY write (create_edge_unstamped, the point #632 stamps), its AUTHORED_BY delete (delete_edge), and its two node writes (create_node, create_node_refs_checked_later, via #635's newly_settles). With a caller established every AUTHORED_BY, author or approver, must name them, and removing someone else's is refused; with nobody established no approver role is added, removed or re-dated and no status moves into settled intent. An unchanged rewrite is not a new signature. Handlers that write several things ask may_sign, the same rule, before their first write. The refusal says who the caller is, how the engine knows, and how an owner signs. The handshake says so on an engine served for others; a local handshake is byte-identical. NOT IN THIS CHANGE: Bearer-token (OIDC) verification on an exposed --http engine, still owed for #616 fix 4.
